overview: Mixtec histories connect distinct kingdoms and ruling families in Oaxaca. Painted manuscripts preserve genealogies and competing political memories alongside rich farming and craft traditions.

items.text: Terraces and irrigation canals supported maize cultivation across varied terrain.
Craftworkers combined turquoise mosaics, gold ornaments and polychrome pottery with intricate figurative designs.
Rattles, scrapers, conch instruments and drums occur in funerary assemblages, indicating music's ceremonial importance.
Codex Bodley traces royal genealogies across the tenth through sixteenth centuries. Its families sometimes opposed one another, making it more than a single dynasty's record.
Bodley's painted deerskin strip folds into pages. Red bands organize the reading of genealogical narratives.
Pohl considers Bodley's painting date unresolved after 1500, potentially early colonial. Related pictorial styles continued in genealogies, maps and land claims.
